title: A Family of Chatterjee's Correlation Coefficients and Their Properties
abstractText: Quantifying the strength of functional dependence between random scalars $X$ and $Y$ is an important statistical problem. While many existing correlation coefficients excel in identifying linear or monotone functional dependence, they fall short in capturing general non-monotone functional relationships. In response, we propose a family of correlation coefficients $ξ^{(h,F)}_n$, characterized by a continuous bivariate function $h$ and a cdf function $F$. By offering a range of selections for $h$ and $F$, $ξ^{(h,F)}_n$ encompasses a diverse class of novel correlation coefficients, while also incorporates the Chatterjee's correlation coefficient (Chatterjee, 2021) as a special case. We prove that $ξ^{(h,F)}_n$ converges almost surely to a deterministic limit $ξ^{(h,F)}$ as sample size $n$ approaches infinity. In addition, under appropriate conditions imposed on $h$ and $F$, the limit $ξ^{(h,F)}$ satisfies the three appealing properties: (P1). it belongs to the range of $[0,1]$; (P2). it equals 1 if and only if $Y$ is a measurable function of $X$; and (P3). it equals 0 if and only if $Y$ is independent of $X$. As amplified by our numerical experiments, our proposals provide practitioners with a variety of options to choose the most suitable correlation coefficient tailored to their specific practical needs.

title: Effect of Trialkyl Borates as Lewis Acids on Quinones for Electrochemical Carbon Dioxide Capture and Concentration
abstractText: Abstract Electrochemical CO2 capture and concentration (eCCC) systems have the potential to operate at efficiencies higher than those of thermal systems. Quinones have been the focus of many eCCC studies as redox carriers, as they can capture or release CO2 depending on their oxidation states. Quinones (Q) with higher cathodic potentials bind CO2 more strongly when they are reduced; however, higher cathodic potentials result in O2 sensitivity. Intra- and intermolecular noncovalent interactions have been explored to anodically shift the second reduction potential (E1/2(Q–1/Q–2)) while maintaining the CO2 binding affinity (log(KCO2)). In this report, we investigate the effects of four trialkyl borate additives, B(OMe)3, B(OEt)3, B(OiPr)3, and B(OBu)3, on the second reduction potential (E1/2(Q–1/Q–2)) and CO2 binding affinity (log(KCO2)) of three quinones, 2-chloro-1,4-benzoquinone (2-ClBQ), 2,3,5,6-tetrafluoro-1,4-benzoquinone (TFQ), and 2,3,5,6-tetrachloro-1,4-benzoquinone (TCQ). Changes in the second reduction potential ranged from 0 to 430 mV with up to 300 equiv of these additives. The magnitude of the anodic shift of the quinones is correlated to the Lewis acidity of the trialkyl borate additive and the Lewis basicity of the quinone. We then investigated the effect of trialkyl borate additives on log(KCO2), which decreases for TFQ and 2-ClBQ but remains constant for TCQ. These results underscore the importance of understanding the additive and quinone interactions in eCCC systems.

title: NanoBlocks: Creating Genetically Encoded Protein Switches Using Competitive Binding
abstractText: Abstract Many regulatory mechanisms function by changing a molecule’s conformation such that it is switched between active and inactive states. Engineering macromolecules such as proteins to show robust conformational changes in response to arbitrary, well-defined molecular stimuli is of great interest in fields such as synthetic biology and nanoscale engineering, because it allows the development of “smart” molecular tools. We present a strategy that can convert “simple” affinity binders such as nanobodies into protein switches that undergo clear structural rearrangements in response to their innate targets, by introducing a peptide that competes for the binding site. We demonstrate proof-of-concept implementations of this “NanoBlock” design by developing genetically encoded fluorescent biosensors based on two entirely different binder frameworks, the ALFA nanobody and the PDZ domain of Erbin. We show that our design allows the construction of well-performing protein switches that can reliably detect their targets in vitro, in mammalian cells, as part of fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) experiments, and that also generalizes to the creation of stimulus-responsive enzymes via the integration of a bioluminescent readout. We furthermore develop a theoretical model that rationalizes the observations and provides insight into the underlying molecular mechanisms. Overall, our strategy expands the possibilities to create “smart” protein-based molecules and effectors.

title: Four-derivative corrections to the neutral-scalar Christodoulou threshold in charged de Sitter black holes
abstractText: Abstract We study leading parity-even four-derivative corrections to the linear Christodoulou regularity criterion for a neutral, massless, minimally coupled spectator scalar in four-dimensional charged de Sitter black holes. We derive the corrected static solution, cold extremality relation, near-horizon geometry, Cauchy-horizon surface gravity, and neutral scalar quasinormal spectrum within Einstein-Maxwell effective theory. Near cold extremality, the scalar equation reduces analytically to the finite-temperature anti-de Sitter two-dimensional throat problem. We find that the dominant nonstationary spherically symmetric mode retains its cold-limit regularity ratio through first order, while higher angular sectors respond to the deformation of the relative throat radii. The finite-distance neutral-scalar Christodoulou boundary nevertheless shifts because the relevant exterior scalar spectrum and the unequal horizon surface gravities enter the regularity ratio. At smaller and intermediate cosmological scales, positive effective coefficients move the Christodoulou threshold to larger normalized separation of the Cauchy and event horizons. Toward the larger cosmological-scale part of the cold branch, the same coefficient directions move that threshold back toward the cold endpoint. The reversal accompanies a transition in the quasinormal family that supplies the spectral gap. We further show that the coefficient combination governing the fixed-charge extremal mass parameter differs generically from those governing the cold throat and the finite-distance neutral-scalar boundary. Extremality therefore does not determine a universal direction for the neutral-scalar Christodoulou-threshold correction. Our results identify cosmological scale and spectral-family competition as essential elements in relating effective gravity, black-hole extremality, and Cauchy-horizon regularity in this spectator sector.

$U$-spin sum rules in charmed baryon decays beyond the $U$-spin limit
abstractText: Abstract $U$-spin symmetry is an important flavor symmetry in studying charmed hadron weak decays. However, the sizeable $U$-spin breaking limits the predictive power of $U$-spin symmetry. In this work, we derive dozens of rate and decay parameter $U$-spin sum rules for charmed baryon decays beyond the exact $U$-spin symmetry limit. These sum rules provide tests of flavor symmetry up to the first-order $U$-spin breaking in the charmed baryon sector.

title: Community Transmission of Pneumonic Plague, Fenoarivobe, Madagascar, 2022
abstractText: The results of an outbreak investigation of pneumonic plague conducted in the plague-endemic district of Fenoarivobe, Madagascar, revealed a familial cluster of plague. Transmission was aided by intrahousehold contact or gatherings and was amplified by delayed plague treatment, highlighting the need for early diagnosis and rapid initiation of appropriate therapy.

title: Peningkatan Kapasitas Kader Posyandu Melalui Lomba Penyuluhan Stunting di Kelureahan Wailiti Kecamatan Alok Barat Kabupaten Sikka
abstractText: Kader posyandu berperan penting dalam edukasi kesehatan dan pencegahan stunting, namun kemampuan komunikasi efektif kader di Kelurahan Wailiti, Kecamatan Alok Barat, Kabupaten Sikka belum optimal. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan meningkatkan kapasitas kader posyandu melalui lomba penyuluhan stunting. Sasaran kegiatan adalah kader yang telah mengikuti pelatihan kompetensi kader dari puskesmas setempat. Metode pelaksanaan meliputi asesmen partisipatif, perencanaan strategi berdasarkan teori achievement motivation dan competitive based learning, persiapan panitia dan juri, sosialisasi, pelaksanaan lomba, serta evaluasi. Lomba diikuti perwakilan dari enam posyandu pada 23 Juli 2026 dengan penilaian yang mencakup penguasaan materi, sistematika penyampaian, teknik komunikasi, dan alat peraga. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan perubahan positif pada kader, yaitu materi disiapkan lebih terstruktur melalui catatan poin, penyampaian lebih sistematis, komunikasi lebih informatif dan persuasif, serta penggunaan alat peraga dari bahan sekitar. Masukan juri turut menjadi umpan balik bagi kader. Dengan demikian, lomba penyuluhan terbukti efektif sebagai metode peningkatan kapasitas kader yang kompetitif sekaligus suportif. Kegiatan ini direkomendasikan untuk dilaksanakan secara berkelanjutan dan direplikasi di wilayah lain.

title: Implementasi Kebijakan Merdeka Belajar Kampus Merdeka melalui Program Surabaya Mengajar di SDN Kebraon II/437 Kota Surabaya
abstractText: Kebijakan Merdeka Belajar Kampus Merdeka (MBKM) diwujudkan di tingkat daerah antara lain melalui Program Surabaya Mengajar (PSM), yaitu skema asistensi mengajar yang menempatkan mahasiswa di sekolah dasar negeri milik Pemerintah Kota Surabaya. Keberhasilan skema ini tidak hanya ditentukan oleh rumusan tujuannya, tetapi juga oleh proses implementasi di sekolah. Penelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan implementasi kebijakan MBKM melalui PSM di SDN Kebraon II/437 Kota Surabaya serta mengidentifikasi faktor pendukung dan penghambatnya berdasarkan enam variabel model Van Meter dan Van Horn. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan data dari observasi, wawancara semi-terstruktur terhadap sembilan informan (satu wakil kepala sekolah bidang kurikulum, empat guru, dan empat mahasiswa peserta), serta dokumentasi. Analisis mengikuti model interaktif Miles dan Huberman dengan triangulasi sumber dan teknik. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa tujuan program dipahami secara umum, tetapi penempatan mahasiswa belum selaras dengan kebutuhan sekolah. Sumber daya dan pendampingan guru memadai untuk kegiatan dasar, namun kapasitas pedagogis mahasiswa non kependidikan terbatas. Komunikasi di tingkat sekolah berjalan intens, sedangkan komunikasi dan pemantauan dari pihak penyelenggara masih umum dan jarang. Lingkungan sosial sekolah bersifat ramah dan disposisi mahasiswa cenderung positif. Kualitas implementasi dengan demikian bertumpu pada mekanisme adaptasi informal di sekolah, sehingga diperlukan penempatan berbasis kebutuhan, petunjuk teknis yang lebih rinci, dan pemantauan lapangan yang terstruktur.

title: Managing the Green Economy through Digital Technologies: Opportunities, Mechanisms, and Prospects
abstractText: This article analyzes the theoretical and methodological foundations, practical mechanisms, and prospects of managing the green economy through digital technologies. The interrelationship between the green economy and digital transformation is examined from the perspective of the "twin transition." The study substantiates the role of artificial intelligence, Big Data, the Internet of Things (IoT), and blockchain technologies in improving energy efficiency, tracking carbon footprints, managing waste, and shaping green finance flows, and proposes institutional mechanisms for their governance. Drawing on a comparative analysis of international experience (the European Union, China, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom, and Singapore) and Uzbekistan's practice, supported by official statistical data, the authors develop an original conceptual model, the "digital-green governance cycle," together with practical recommendations for managing the digital-green transition in Uzbekistan. The research methodology combines systems analysis, a comparative-historical approach, and the generalization of statistical data.

title: Pengaruh Lingkungan Kerja Fisik, Beban Kerja dan Kompensasi Terhadap Kinerja Karyawan pada PT. Musim Mas
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh lingkungan kerja fisik, beban kerja, dan kompensasi terhadap kinerja karyawan divisi produksi PT. Musim Mas Medan. Penelitian kuantitatif asosiatif ini melibatkan populasi 212 karyawan tetap, dan sampel sebanyak 68 responden ditentukan dengan rumus Slovin pada tingkat kesalahan 10%. Data primer dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner skala Likert lima poin yang telah lolos uji validitas dan reliabilitas, didukung wawancara, observasi, dan dokumentasi. Data dianalisis dengan statistik deskriptif, uji asumsi klasik, regresi linear berganda, uji t, uji F, dan koefisien determinasi. Lingkungan kerja fisik (X1) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kinerja karyawan (B = 0,356; t = 3,502; p = 0,001). Beban kerja (X2) memiliki koefisien positif, tetapi tidak signifikan (B = 0,187; t = 1,297; p = 0,199). Kompensasi (X3) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan (B = 0,284; t = 2,999; p = 0,004). Secara simultan, model yang memuat X1, X2, dan X3 signifikan (F = 75,727; p < 0,001) dengan R² = 0,780 dan adjusted R² = 0,770. Temuan ini menempatkan perbaikan kondisi fisik area produksi dan kejelasan sistem kompensasi sebagai prioritas peningkatan kinerja karyawan.

Attitude and acceptability of IVF add-ons to improve reproductive outcomes: a focus group qualitative study
abstractText: Abstract STUDY QUESTION What factors are important for patients when evaluating the efficacy, safety, cost, and acceptability of IVF add-ons? SUMMARY ANSWER Although efficacy is the most important factor for patients, interim markers of success can also be important. WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY IVF add-ons are increasingly offered alongside assisted conception despite limited evidence of their efficacy, safety, or value for money. Capturing patient perspectives on their acceptability and outcome priorities is essential to guide ethical clinical practice and inform future research. STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION Three online focus groups were conducted with 12 people who had used assisted reproductive technologies and were not currently in treatment. The focus groups were conducted in small groups of three to five people with each focus group lasting ∼2 h. PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS Participants were recruited through fertility charities and patient advocacy groups. All 12 participants were women and lived in the UK. All were currently in a relationship, and most had prior experience of using IVF add-ons. Online focus groups were conducted to discuss views on the efficacy, safety, and acceptability of IVF add-ons, and to identify preferred outcomes. MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE Nearly all participants defined the most important outcome of using an add-on to be achieving a live birth. However, they recognized that a live birth could feel a distant endpoint within the IVF treatment and therefore valued interim milestones as indicators of success. The main theme found in relation to understanding the risks involved was the need for patients to balance risk with desperation to have a baby. In terms of cost, two themes emerged, the need to balance cost with needing money for future treatments and the differing views on what is an acceptable cost. When receiving information about add-ons, participants reflected on the importance of finding reputable sources while also having to navigate conflicting information. Overall, the effectiveness of an add-on was valued over cost and safety, although cost and the risk of regret remained important considerations in decision-making. Most participants would not regret using add-ons, although some said they may regret not having used them. LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION All participants were women, and most were White. Findings may not be applicable to other populations. WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS Capturing participants’ views on efficacy, safety, cost, and acceptability is essential not only to guide future research priorities but also to inform ethical clinical practice and policy. By incorporating patient perspectives, future trials can ensure that outcomes reflect what matters most to those undergoing treatment, thereby improving the relevance and impact of research in reproductive medicine. FUNDING AFFINITY is funded by a public research grant from the National Institute for Health and Care Research's (NIHR) Efficacy and Mechanism Evaluation (EME) programme—Award ID NIHR168789. DISCLOSURES The authors have no conflict of interest to declare. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER N/A.

title: Analisis Biaya pada UMKM Mukena Rendi Collection
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis struktur biaya produksi, menghitung Harga Pokok Produksi (HPP) menggunakan metode Full Costing dan Variable Costing, menetapkan titik impas (Break Even Point/BEP), serta mengevaluasi efisiensi dan pengambilan keputusan bisnis pada UMKM Mukena Rendi Collection. Penelitian ini merupakan penelitian deskriptif kuantitatif yang berfokus pada analisis data biaya produksi dengan volume pembuatan sebanyak 5.000 set mukena per bulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa total biaya produksi untuk 5.000 unit mukena adalah sebesar Rp311.516.000. Komponen biaya terbesar didominasi oleh biaya bahan baku langsung sebesar Rp169.016.000 (±54%) dan biaya tenaga kerja langsung sebesar Rp140.000.000 (±45%), sementara biaya overhead pabrik (BOP) sebesar Rp2.500.000. Perhitungan HPP per unit menghasilkan nilai Rp62.303 dengan metode Full Costing dan Rp61.803 dengan metode Variable Costing. Selisih sebesar Rp500 per unit dipengaruhi oleh alokasi biaya tetap overhead pabrik pada metode Full Costing. Dengan harga jual produk sebesar Rp70.000 per unit, diperoleh margin kontribusi sebesar Rp8.197 per unit dan total laba sebesar Rp40.985.000. Analisis Break Even Point menunjukkan titik impas tercapai pada tingkat penjualan 305 unit, yang mengindikasikan tingkat produksi 5.000 unit berada pada area yang sangat aman dan efisien. Pada studi pengambilan keputusan pesanan khusus sebanyak 1.000 unit dengan harga tawaran Rp65.000 per unit, analisis Variable Costing menyimpulkan pesanan tersebut layak diterima karena menghasilkan tambahan kontribusi margin positif sebesar Rp3.197.000 tanpa menambah biaya tetap.

title: PENGEMBANGAN MODEL MANAJEMEN MUTU PENDIDIKAN BERBASIS NILAI ISLAM MELALUI AUDIT, EVALUASI, BENCHMARKING, DAN AKREDITASI
abstractText: Improving the quality of Islamic education requires a quality management approach that is not only oriented toward meeting established standards but also grounded in Islamic values, including trustworthiness (amanah), justice (‘adl), excellence (ihsan), consultation (shura), and continuous improvement. This article focuses on synthesizing quality management principles with Islamic educational values and developing a quality management model that systematically integrates audit, self-evaluation, benchmarking, and accreditation. This study employs a qualitative approach using a literature review method. The research stages include identifying and selecting relevant literature, analyzing the concepts of quality management and Islamic educational values, synthesizing relevant principles, and formulating an Islamic education quality management model. The findings indicate that integrating Islamic values with quality management principles can establish a quality assurance system that goes beyond compliance with standards toward fostering an ethical, integrity-based, and sustainable quality culture. Audits function as instruments for assessment and control, self-evaluation as a reflective process for identifying institutional achievements and weaknesses, benchmarking as a means of learning from best practices, and accreditation as formal recognition of quality standards compliance. The proposed model positions Islamic values as its philosophical foundation, quality management as its organizational framework, and the four instruments as mechanisms for continuous quality improvement. Therefore, the model provides a conceptual framework for developing Islamic education quality management that is integrative, adaptive, sustainable, and oriented toward public benefit.

title: Agnuside from Vitex negundo L. Attenuates Hepatocellular Lipid Accumulation: Association with the AMPK/SREBP1/FASN/HMGCR/PPARα/UCP2 Signaling Network
abstractText: Abstract Vitex negundo L. (VN) is a medicinal plant known for its anti-inflammatory and hepatoprotective properties, commonly used as a vegetable in northeastern Indian communities. However, its role in treating nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is still underexplored. This study evaluates the therapeutic potential of VN and its bioactive compounds in reducing lipid accumulation in CC1 hepatocytes. A crude extract of VN and its n-butanol fraction (VNBU) were tested on palmitate-induced CC1 hepatocytes to evaluate lipid accumulation. Key compounds Agnuside, 5-hydroxy-3,6,7,3́,4́-pentamethoxyflavone, and Vitexilactone were isolated. Agnuside’s effects on lipogenesis, cholesterol accumulation, and fatty acid oxidation were assessed using biochemical assays and Western blot analysis. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations were conducted to explore its interactions with 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (HMGCR). Agnuside treatment was associated with reduced lipid accumulation by modulating Adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK), HMGCR, Sterol regulatory element-binding transcription factor 1 (SREBP1), Fatty acid synthase (FASN), Peroxisome Proliferator-activated receptors (PPARα), and uncoupling protein (UCP2), suggesting a favorable shift in lipid metabolism. Computational studies indicated that Agnuside binds stably to HMGCR, similar to statins. In summary, these findings suggest that VN and Agnuside exert protective effects in hepatocytes, accompanied by favorable shifts in lipid metabolism markers. Further studies are needed to confirm the causal role of this signaling network.

abstractText: Abstract Two previously undescribed monoterpenoid bisindole alkaloids, kopsiyunnanines O1 and P, were isolated from Kopsia arborea (Apocynaceae) and structurally characterized. These two bisindoles are composed of eburnamine- and rhazidigenine-related monomeric units and differ in substituents attached to C-7′ of the rhazidigenine-related unit. Furthermore, kopsiyunnanine O2 was identified as an interconvertible isomer of kopsiyunnanine O1. The reversible interconversion between kopsiyunnanines O1 and O2 was influenced by the solvent and the addition of acid.

title: A dynamic modeling framework for metro network resilience assessment and improvement under extreme rainstorm disasters
abstractText: Abstract Extreme rainstorms can severely disrupt metro systems through station inundation, passenger-flow redistribution, secondary overloads, and prolonged service disruption. Despite advances in metro vulnerability and resilience research, hazard exposure, direct disruption, passenger rerouting, and load-induced degradation are often modeled separately, while resilience assessment rarely integrates infrastructure availability, transport efficiency, and satisfied passenger demand. Recovery is also commonly treated as an external schedule rather than a feedback process, although station reopening may redistribute flows and trigger renewed overload. To address these limitations, this study develops a dynamic modeling framework for metro network resilience assessment and improvement across the disruption–recovery process. The metro system is represented as a time-dependent weighted network integrating rainstorm hazard, rainfall-triggered station failures, passenger rerouting, flow-induced cascading degradation, network-state evolution, performance evaluation, and recovery intervention. System performance is measured using a composite indicator of passenger service ratio, network efficiency, and station availability, while resilience is characterized through stage-based capacities and cumulative performance loss. For resilience improvement, resource-constrained recovery decisions are formulated, and a stability-screened performance-gain strategy that prioritizes stations by marginal benefit is compared with a no-intervention reference scenario. An illustrative application to a simplified Shenzhen Metro subnetwork under a normalized rainstorm scenario reproduces the progression from direct failures to cascading disruption, performance deterioration, and recovery. Sensitivity analyses further show consistent and interpretable responses to variations in station-capacity buffers, direct-failure thresholds, and recovery budgets. The framework provides a computationally tractable and transferable basis for dynamic resilience analysis, and practical recovery planning in rainstorm-exposed metro systems.

A Study on Nail Art Works Using Natural Fractal Motifs Based on Generative AI
abstractText: This study aimed to develop nail art designs inspired by natural fractal motifs and compare the visual expression of DALL·E, Midjourney, and Stable Diffusion. Four natural fractal motifs were selected through a literature review: clouds, lightning, ant nests, and planets. A shared prompt framework incorporating fractal characteristics, formative elements, and nail art design requirements was established. Common English prompts were used as initial inputs for the three models, followed by image refinement using their respective functions. A focus group interview (FGI) with ten nail art professionals and instructors was conducted to examine design suitability and practical applicability. The generated images exhibited differences in composition, color, texture, and detail. FGI participants highlighted Midjourney’s representation of fractal elements, color harmony, texture rendering, and overall design quality. Their feedback informed the selection of Midjourney for physical artwork development. Four nail art works were produced, incorporating randomness and overlapping, nonlinearity and diffusion, irregularity and distortion, and an artistic interpretation of self-similarity and repetition. The visual features of the generated images were adapted to the materials and techniques used in physical production. This study presents a design development process integrating motif analysis, prompt design, image generation, FGI, and physical production. The findings suggest that generative AI can support the exploration of fractal-inspired nail art and offer a foundation for further applications in beauty design and education.

Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy in pediatric kikuchi-fujimoto disease: a retrospective case series
abstractText: Abstract Background Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease (KFD) is a rare, self-limiting cause of cervical lymphadenopathy in children, frequently misdiagnosed as malignant lymphoma or systemic lupus erythematosus, which may prompt invasive diagnostic procedures. We aimed to describe the clinicopathological findings and procedure-related complications in a retrospective case series of pediatric patients with KFD diagnosed by US-CNB. Methods We retrospectively reviewed medical records of 20 pediatric patients (≤ 18 years) diagnosed with KFD via US-CNB who met the study inclusion criteria between January 2016 and December 2025. All procedures were performed under local anesthesia using an 18-gauge automated biopsy gun. We described which histopathological and immunohistochemical analyses were possible in the available core specimens. Complications and clinical outcomes were recorded during a minimum 30-day follow-up. Results The cohort included 14 males and 6 females, with a median age of 9.1 years (range: 2–16). title: Strategic Consistency and Structural Fairness in Dynamic Efficiency Evaluation: The Inertial Cross-Efficiency Malmquist Productivity Index
abstractText: Cross-efficiency-based Malmquist productivity measurement involves both the selection of DEA-optimal weights across Malmquist states and the aggregation of heterogeneous peer assessments. This study develops the Inertial Cross-Efficiency Malmquist Productivity Index (I-CEMPI). The method retains the state-specific primary-optimal weighting sets and coordinates the four Malmquist states through minimum intertemporal adjustment, yielding a unique and reproducible weight representation while preserving primary DEA optimality. Peer Cross-Malmquist assessments are subsequently combined through strategic-perspective-balanced geometric aggregation, which preserves the multiplicative decomposition into efficiency change and technical change. Applying I-CEMPI to 440 listed Chinese SRDI “Little Giant” enterprises over 2019–2024 shows substantial scope for intertemporal selection within the empirical optimal sets. Perspective balancing produces larger changes in aggregate productivity assessments than intertemporal coordination, while comparisons with the standard MPI and a published Cross-GMPI show high overall agreement together with differences in a subset of firm-level classifications. Innovation productivity contracts over most horizons, with technical change accounting for the larger share of cumulative contraction. Strategic perspectives differ more clearly in their efficiency-change and technical-change compositions than in persistent aggregate productivity rankings.

title: Waste-derived feedstocks and industrial microwave drying influence antioxidant capacity and immune-associated protein composition in black soldier fly larvae (Hermetia illucens)
abstractText: Abstract Black soldier fly larvae ( Hermetia illucens ) are increasingly used as a sustainable protein source in animal feeds. Beyond macronutrient value, black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) contain antioxidant compounds and immune-associated proteins that may contribute to their functional value. However, the extent to which rearing substrate and processing influence these components remains poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of feedstock and industrial microwave drying on antioxidant capacity and immune-associated protein composition in BSFL. Larvae were reared on three waste-derived feedstocks (fruit and vegetable waste, soy okara and brewer’s spent grain). Antioxidant capacity was measured using Folin-Ciocalteu, FRAP and DPPH assays. Immune-associated proteins and AMP candidates were characterised using LC-MS/MS proteomics. Industrial microwave drying was evaluated relative to freeze-drying. Antioxidant capacity differed significantly among feedstocks (ANOVA, ). Brewer’s spent grain increased total phenolic content and reducing capacity, while fruit and vegetable waste resulted in the highest radical scavenging activity. Total immune protein richness did not differ among diets; however, immune functional composition varied significantly (PERMANOVA, R 2 = 0.907, ). Larvae reared on fruit and vegetable waste showed increased representation of immune effector proteins and higher AMP candidate richness. Industrial microwave drying resulted in a 43% reduction in detectable immune-associated proteins and reduced antioxidant capacity. These findings demonstrate that feedstock and processing shape the composition and detectability of antioxidant and immune-associated components in BSFL biomass, highlighting opportunities to optimise insect-derived feed ingredients for targeted applications.

abstractText: Abstract Occupational respiratory disease (ORD) surveillance remains largely reactive, with diagnosis often occurring only after clinically significant symptoms develop. Existing risk stratification tools are primarily clinically derived and rarely incorporate occupational exposure variables such as exposure intensity, duration, and workplace hazards, limiting early identification of at-risk workers. This review synthesizes current evidence on predictive modelling and risk stratification tools for respiratory diseases, evaluates their applicability to occupational health, and proposes a data-driven framework for proactive risk stratification. A structured literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between 2021 and 2025. Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) and free-text terms related to occupational respiratory diseases, predictive modelling, prognostic tools, and occupational exposure assessment were combined using Boolean operators. Extracted data included study characteristics, modelling approaches, predictors, and model performance metrics, which were narratively synthesized using thematic mapping. Of 618 records identified, six representative evidence approaches were retained for detailed comparative synthesis. Clinical models such as BODE and DOSE provided useful prognostic information but lacked occupational exposure parameters. Exposure-based approaches showed associations between cumulative exposure and respiratory outcomes, while a meta-analysis of machine-learning models for acute respiratory distress syndrome reported a pooled AUC of 0.7407. Key predictors included age, smoking status, lung function, and exposure-related factors. Current reactive and clinically focused approaches limit effective ORD prevention. Integrating occupational exposure variables into predictive, data-driven risk stratification frameworks is essential for early identification of high-risk workers. The proposed ORDiRS framework represents a step toward proactive occupational health surveillance in industrial settings.

abstractText: The Dunning-Kruger effect is an underrecognized challenge in neurocritical care, where novice clinicians' overconfidence can harm patient outcomes. title: Deciphering the Contribution of Bacterial Biofilms to Persistent Chronic Infections and Multidrug Antibiotic Resistance Mechanisms
abstractText: Bacterial biofilms are organized microbial communities that attach to living or nonliving surfaces and become embedded in a self-produced extracellular matrix composed of polysaccharides, proteins, and extracellular DNA. This growth pattern promotes survival under adverse environmental conditions and contributes to the persistence of infections. This overview examines biofilm development, mechanisms underlying reduced antibiotic susceptibility, and approaches to preventing and controlling biofilm-associated infections. Biofilm formation generally proceeds through initial surface attachment, irreversible adhesion, microcolony formation, maturation into a three-dimensional structure, and dispersal of cells capable of colonizing additional surfaces. Adhesion molecules, extracellular matrix production, and quorum-sensing systems contribute to the establishment and organization of biofilms in many pathogenic bacteria. Biofilms are clinically important because of their association with chronic infections and infections involving implanted medical devices. Their persistence reflects several interacting mechanisms, including limited penetration of some antibiotics, altered bacterial metabolic activity, and the presence of dormant persister cells. Biofilm communities can also facilitate the transfer of genes that confer antibiotic resistance. Biofilm-associated antibiotic tolerance and genetically mediated resistance represent distinct mechanisms, both of which can complicate bacterial eradication. Preventive and therapeutic approaches include antimicrobial surface coatings, combination antibiotic therapy, enzymatic disruption of the extracellular matrix, and removal of contaminated medical devices when clinically indicated. Emerging approaches, including nanotechnology-based interventions and bacteriophage therapy, offer additional possibilities but require further evaluation of their effectiveness and applicability. The discussion highlights the importance of addressing bacterial cells, the protective matrix, and colonized surfaces when developing biofilm-control strategies. Further research should clarify how these approaches can be integrated to improve the prevention and management of persistent biofilm-associated infections.

title: Twist-Dependent In-Plane Symmetry Breaking in the WSe2/Black Phosphorus Interface
abstractText: Abstract The control of optical responses and electronic states via the twist angle, “twistronics”, has revolutionized the research field of van der Waals heterostructures. Despite extensive advances in twisted interfaces composed of materials sharing identical or similar crystal symmetries, twist-dependent phenomena at symmetry-mismatched interfaces hosting unconventional moiré superlattices and symmetry breaking remain poorly understood. Here, we report twist-dependent in-plane symmetry breaking at a symmetry-mismatched heterointerface between WSe2 and black phosphorus. Employing polarization-resolved second-harmonic generation (SHG) microscopy, we characterize the systematic evolution of in-plane symmetry breaking in WSe2/black phosphorus interfaces by varying the twist angle. We propose the twist-dependent in-plane polarization as a possible interpretation, supported by theoretical model calculations and their good agreement with the observed evolution of the SHG response. Our findings extend twistronics to symmetry-mismatched interfaces, offering a strategy to engineer nonlinear optical responses and interfacial polarization in low-symmetry van der Waals systems.

title: Toward a Cross-Pathway Susceptibility Profile for Urinary Tract Infection After Pelvic Floor Reconstruction
abstractText: AIM: Urinary tract infection (UTI) is a frequent early complication after pelvic floor reconstruction. This study examined whether perioperative UTI is associated primarily with the surgical approach or with recurring patient-, disease-, and care-related factors. METHODS: Medical records were retrospectively reviewed for 376 women treated with pelvic floor reconstructive surgery from 2020 through 2025. According to the principal reconstructive procedure, the cohort was divided into three surgical strata: mesh-based sacrospinous fixation accompanied by transobturator tape (TOT) or tension-free vaginal tape (TVT) insertion; combined anterior and posterior colporrhaphy with a midurethral sling; and anterior and posterior colporrhaphy performed without an associated sling procedure. The study endpoint was a symptomatic urinary tract infection confirmed by urine culture during the initial hospital admission. Associations between candidate predictors and infection were estimated separately within each surgical stratum. Stratum-level effect estimates were then integrated using a DerSimonian–Laird random-effects model to obtain pooled odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Cross-stratum variability was quantified through Cochran’s Q test and the I2 statistic. RESULTS: Of the 376 women included, 71 experienced a symptomatic, culture-confirmed infection during the perioperative period, producing an overall event rate of 18.9%. The proportion of affected patients varied numerically among the three reconstructive pathways, although no statistically significant difference was observed in the unadjusted comparison. When risk estimates were synthesized across surgical strata, higher odds of infection were observed in postmenopausal women, patients older than 63 years, those with grade III–IV pelvic organ prolapse, women with morbid obesity, patients requiring bladder catheterization for more than 3 days, and those undergoing hysterectomy during the same operation. The principal significant associations showed little or no between-stratum heterogeneity, suggesting a consistent direction of association across surgical approaches, although the limited number of subgroups (k = 3) and instances of non-estimable models restrict definitive conclusions regarding reproducibility; further validation in larger cohorts is warranted. CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative urinary tract infection after pelvic floor reconstructive surgery appears to reflect a multifactorial susceptibility profile, influenced mainly by patient characteristics, prolapse severity, and prolonged catheterization rather than procedure type alone. These findings support individualized risk assessment and reduced unnecessary catheter use. However, differences in baseline characteristics between surgical groups preclude concluding that the procedures carry equivalent infectious risk.

In addition, the study aims to find out whether there are differences between the six-dimensional strategy and the traditional teaching method in the development of the performance of the handball skills in the post-test. It also compares the results of these two methods of teaching on enhancing students decision making after the educational program. The researcher used the experimental method because of its appropriateness that has been considered in light of the nature and objective of the study. The research sample consisted of two physical education second year student sections at the College of Physical Education and Sports Sciences, University of Mosul and selected randomly. The experimental group was Section (C) and Control group was Section (Y). Prior to education program implementation, homogeneity and equivalence of the two groups was achieved. The researcher examined the approved handball curriculum of the second-year students in the first semester of the academic year and then developed an educational program based on the strategy of six dimensions. The program was consisted of 12 educational units which were implemented in the experimental group while the control group received conventional teaching method. Appropriate educational resources and instructional technologies were also used by the researcher that was needed for the experiment. The researcher used several research instruments, such as the preliminary information form, the skill acquisition assessment and decision-making scale, to gather the necessary data. The results showed that the experimental group had a significantly higher level of skill acquisition and performance than the control group. The findings also showed that the 6D strategy is effective in the promotion of skill achievement than the conventional teaching method. Furthermore, the results of the students in the experimental program showed that the six-dimensional strategy had a positive effect in enhancing the students' decision making ability, as evidenced by the better results obtained in the decision making assessment. Improvements were observed across the seven targeted professional competence dimensions. These findings provide initial empirical support for OBALM as a structured learning approach that integrates outcome-based learning, authentic problems, practical performance, feedback, and reflection in vocational higher education. title: Tenecteplase for acute ischemic stroke: from an alteplase alternative toward workflow-oriented thrombolysis
abstractText: Tenecteplase has emerged as a practical, evidence-supported thrombolytic alternative for acute ischemic stroke, challenging the long-standing predominance of alteplase. Greater fibrin specificity, resistance to plasminogen activator inhibitor-1, a longer half-life, and single-bolus administration provide a strong pharmacologic rationale for its use in time-sensitive stroke care. Accumulating evidence from randomized trials and meta-analyses suggests that tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg is a reasonable alternative to alteplase for eligible patients treated within 4.5 hours, with particular practical advantages for those with large vessel occlusion who may require transfer for endovascular thrombectomy. Recent trials have broadened the discussion to include imaging-selected treatment beyond the conventional time window and adjunctive intra-arterial administration after thrombectomy. However, implementation varies across regions, and regulatory approval, reimbursement, safety concerns, and limited real-world data from Asia continue to shape clinical adoption. This review examines the pharmacologic rationale, clinical trial evidence, evolving guidelines, workflow implications, and unresolved questions surrounding tenecteplase for acute ischemic stroke, focusing on its potential role in Asian stroke systems.

title: Effects of Combined Leonurus japonicus and Trichosanthes kirilowii Extracts on Anti-Inflammatory, Antimicrobial, and Skin Thermoregulatory Activities
abstractText: Purpose: This study aimed to evaluate the potential of a complex extract containing Leonurus japonicus (LS) and Trichosanthes kirilowii (TKR) as a natural functional cosmetic ingredient by investigating its effects on inflammatory responses in macrophages, the proliferation of skin resident bacteria, and variations in skin temperature.Methods: The anti-inflammatory efficacy was analyzed by measuring NO production and the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines, specifically TNF-α and IL-1β, in LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages. Antibacterial activity was assessed against Staphylococcus epidermidis, a prominent skin resident and opportunistic pathogen. Additionally, clinical evaluations were conducted to monitor changes in skin temperature immediately and at specific intervals following topical application.Results: The complex extract effectively inhibited NO production and suppressed the expression of TNF-α and IL-1β in a dose-dependent manner, confirming its ability to block inflammatory mediators. In the antibacterial assays, the growth of S. epidermidis was significantly inhibited in proportion to the concentration, with both LS and the LS+TKR complex exhibiting a potent inhibition rate of over 90% at a concentration of 100 ㎍/㎖. These results indicate a superior antibacterial synergy compared to single treatments. Furthermore, clinical measurements demonstrated a significant reduction in skin temperature post-application. This thermal reduction is consistent with the scientific mechanism wherein decreased skin temperature leads to reduced sebum secretion and microbial metabolic rates, thereby enhancing overall antibacterial efficacy and stabilizing skin exposed to thermal stress.Conclusion: In conclusion, the complex extract of Leonurus japonicus and Trichosanthes kirilowii demonstrated a functional synergy exceeding that of individual components. By simultaneously providing macrophage-based anti-inflammatory action, skin temperature regulation, and robust antibacterial activity, this complex extract holds significant promise as a multifunctional natural material for improving acne-prone and sensitive skin conditions.

Deep learning predicts IDH1 mutation status in acute myeloid leukemia from bone marrow smears
abstractText: Abstract Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with IDH1 mutations is amenable to targeted therapy, highlighting the need for reliable identification. We developed an attention-based multiple-instance learning model to predict IDH1 mutation status using bone marrow smear whole-slide images from 436 AML patients across four centers in Germany and the US, achieving a mean single pooled ROC-AUC of 0.81. In top tile analysis, model predictions for IDH1 were associated with immature leukemia phenotypes.

Performance of Floating Chart in Utilization of Small Pelagic Fish Resources in Makassar Strait Waters, Donggala, Central Sulawesi
abstractText: Small-scale capture fisheries are important for utilizing small pelagic fish resources and sustaining coastal livelihoods. This study analyzes the effects of fishermen’s capabilities and operational effectiveness on small pelagic fish resource utilization and floating lift net performance in the Makassar Strait waters off Sabang Village, Balaesang District, Donggala Regency, Central Sulawesi, Indonesia. A quantitative explanatory approach with a cross-sectional design was employed. Primary data were collected from 300 fishermen directly involved in floating lift net operations using a structured five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS. The results show that fishermen’s capabilities positively affect operational effectiveness, resource utilization, and floating lift net performance. Operational effectiveness positively affects resource utilization but has no significant direct effect on floating lift net performance at the 5% level. Resource utilization positively affects performance and serves as a key mediating mechanism linking fishermen’s capabilities and operational effectiveness to performance. The model explains 42.5% of the variance in floating lift net performance. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening fishermen’s capabilities, improving operational effectiveness, and promoting productive, selective, and sustainable resource utilization.

title: Quality and readability of large language model–generated responses on type 2 diabetes remission: a cross-sectional balanced factorial study
abstractText: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for patient education and medical information delivery. However, their outputs may involve trade-offs among medical accuracy, comprehensiveness, empathy, and readability. Type 2 diabetes remission is a clinically nuanced concept that is readily misunderstood by patients, making it a suitable context in which to evaluate both the medical quality and patient accessibility of artificial intelligence–generated health information. To systematically compare the medical quality and readability of responses concerning type 2 diabetes remission generated by different LLMs and prompting strategies, and to characterize their joint quality–readability profiles. We conducted a cross-sectional study using a balanced factorial design. Responses were generated for 16 core questions concerning type 2 diabetes remission using 4 LLMs—DeepSeek-V3.2,GPT-5.5,Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Sonnet 4.6—and 6 prompting strategies: Keyword, Question, 6th-grade, Guideline, Patient, and Doctor. This yielded 384 AI-generated responses. Two endocrinologists, each with more than 5 years of clinical experience, independently evaluated medical quality using a prespecified rubric. Five domains—Accuracy, Relevance, Comprehensiveness, Empathy, and Falsehood avoidance—were rated on 5-point ordinal scales. A descriptive Composite quality score was also calculated. Readability was assessed using the Flesch Reading Ease Score (FRES), Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL), Gunning Fog Index (GFOG), and Simple Measure of Gobbledygook (SMOG). Quality ratings were analyzed using cumulative link mixed models, whereas readability outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models; Question ID was included as a random intercept in all models. Exploratory analyses examined Spearman correlations between readability and quality and identified Pareto-efficient model–prompt combinations. All 384 responses were included in the analysis, with no missing data. The descriptive Composite quality score ranged from 4.175 for Gemini 3.1 Pro to 4.285 for DeepSeek-V3.2 across models and from 4.066 for the 6th-grade strategy to 4.350 for the Doctor strategy across prompting strategies. Cumulative link mixed models showed significant main effects of model across all 5 quality domains: Accuracy (LR χ² = 10.964, LR-based pseudo-R² = 0.0281, 95% CI 0.0015–0.0636, P = 0.012), Relevance (LR χ² = 54.042, LR-based pseudo-R² = 0.1313, 95% CI 0.0688–0.1974, P < 0.001), Comprehensiveness (LR χ² = 12.018, LR-based pseudo-R² = 0.0308, 95% CI 0.0025–0.0677, P = 0.007), Empathy (LR χ² = 50.905, LR-based pseudo-R² = 0.1242, 95% CI 0.0632–0.1890, P < 0.001), and Falsehood avoidance (LR χ² = 18.752, LR-based pseudo-R² = 0.0477, 95% CI 0.0107–0.0922, P < 0.001). Prompting strategy also showed significant main effects across the quality domains, with the largest effect observed for Empathy (LR χ² = 243.836, LR-based pseudo-R² = 0.4701, 95% CI 0.3786–0.5477, P < 0.001). Descriptively, GPT-5.5 had the numerically highest mean scores for Accuracy (4.448) and Falsehood avoidance (4.469), whereas DeepSeek-V3.2 had the numerically highest mean scores for Relevance (4.948), Comprehensiveness (4.427), and Empathy (3.615). Among prompting strategies, Patient had the numerically highest mean Empathy score (4.359), whereas Doctor had the numerically highest mean Comprehensiveness score (4.609). For readability, both model and prompting strategy showed significant main effects on FRES, FKGL, GFOG, and SMOG. DeepSeek-V3.2 had the numerically highest mean FRES (51.28), whereas Claude Sonnet 4.6 had the lowest (32.98); among prompting strategies, 6th-grade had the numerically highest mean FRES (69.70), whereas Doctor had the lowest (27.50). In an exploratory response-level correlation analysis that did not account for clustering within Question ID and was intended for hypothesis generation only, FRES was positively correlated with Empathy (ρ = 0.53) and negatively correlated with Comprehensiveness, Falsehood avoidance, and the Composite quality score (ρ = −0.46, − 0.40, and − 0.26, respectively; FDR-adjusted q < 0.001), indicating directionally divergent association patterns between readability and different dimensions of medical quality. In patient-education responses related to type 2 diabetes remission, LLM output performance was influenced by both model choice and prompting strategy. No single model–prompt combination consistently outperformed the others across all evaluated outcomes. Within the T2DM remission question set examined in this study, response optimization required trade-offs among accuracy, comprehensiveness, readability, falsehood avoidance, and empathy.

abstractText: Cel pracy Celem artykułu jest analiza motywacji, oczekiwań i obaw funkcjonariuszy oraz kandydatów do służby, ze szczególnym uwzględnieniem zgodności między oficjalnym systemem motywacyjnym a rzeczywistymi doświadczeniami pracowników. Materiał i metody Źródłem wiedzy na temat motywacji pracowników są wyniki badań empirycznych przeprowadzonych z wykorzystaniem metody sondażu diagnostycznego. Jako technikę badawczą zastosowano anonimową ankietę kwestionariuszową skierowaną do funkcjonariuszy oraz kandydatów do służby. Wyniki Stopień dopasowania systemu motywacyjnego SW do potrzeb pracowników i kandydatów jest częściowy. Dobrze adresowane są kwestie stabilności finansowej i formalnej ścieżki kariery. Niedostatecznie ujęto wartości związane z rozwojem osobistym, misją społeczną i równowagą życiową – szczególnie istotne dla młodszych kandydatów. Funkcjonariusze wskazują na realne problemy organizacyjne, które obniżają skuteczność systemu motywacyjnego (brak uznania, nadmierna dyscyplina, biurokracja). Natomiast znacznie większe rozbieżności można zauważyć w przypadku analizy obaw i zagrożeń, związanych z pełnieniem służby. Kluczowe wydaje się połączenie możliwości rozwoju, wsparcia w budowaniu kompetencji społecznych oraz zapewnienia stabilnych i przewidywalnych warunków pracy. title: Different profiles of sleep disturbances in early-stage neurocognitive diseases: a prospective cohort study
abstractText: Abstract Background Alzheimer’sdisease (AD), behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia bvFTD, and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) are all associated with sleep disturbances; however, reports on the prevalence of sleep disorders or symptoms in the early stages of these diseases are limited. Our goal was to assess the prevalence of sleep disturbances and characterize different sleep disturbance profiles in early-stage AD, bvFTD and DLB. Methods A total of 111 early-stage patients including 60 AD (mean age 64.3), 35 bvFTD (mean age 62.4), and 16 DLB cases (mean age 71.1), along with 63 cognitively healthy controls (HC, mean age 59.0), were prospectively recruited from Kuopio and Oulu University Hospitals. Early-stage was determined by Clinical Dementia Rating Scale (CDR) global score 0–1. Sleep disturbances were evaluated using the Basic Nordic Sleep Questionnaire (BNSQ), focusing on characterization of prior sleep habits, sleep disorders, and sleep-related (hypnotic) drug usage. Results DLB patients showed the highest overall burden of sleep disturbances relative to other groups. When bvFTD was compared to AD, patients with bvFTD reported more apneas during sleep than AD (18% % vs. 4%, p = 0.024, OR = 0.17, 95% Cl 0.03–0.92). When compared to HC, patients with bvFTD exhibited fewer nighttime awakenings (44% vs. 71%, p = 0.003, OR = 0.22, 95% CI 0.08–0.59) and reported about one hour more sleep per day (8.46 h vs. 7.59 h, General linear model, p = 0.020, B = -0.70), similar to findings in AD (8.40 h vs. General linear model, 7.59 h, p = 0.001, B = -0.78). No significant differences in total sleep duration were observed between disease groups. Conclusions Sleep disturbance profiles differed across disease groups at an early stage, but when compared to HC differences were modest. These findings suggest sleep disturbances may be present in early disease stage.

title: Using Gemini Voice-To-Text in Facilitating Pronunciation Awareness Through Self-Correction Among Eighth-Grade Students
abstractText: This study aims to investigate how Gemini Voice-to-Text facilitates pronunciation awareness through self-correction among eighth-grade students in an English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classroom context. Specifically, it examines students’ experiences using the tool, how AI-generated transcription supports their awareness of pronunciation differences, and the practical benefits and challenges experienced during implementation. This study used a qualitative case study design. The participants in the study were eight eighth-grade students from SMP Negeri 16 Surabaya, East Java, Indonesia. These students participated in pronunciation activities using Gemini Voice-to-Text. Data were collected through classroom observation, semi-structured interviews, and documentation of the AI-generated transcription output. Analysis of the collected data was conducted thematically with data familiarization, coding, categorization, and developing themes. The findings revealed that students used Gemini Voice-to-Text through three interconnected processes: accessing the tool during speaking activities, reviewing AI-generated transcription, and comparing their spoken production with the recognized output. These processes provided students with opportunities to notice pronunciation differences and engage in self-correction through repetition and modification of their pronunciation. Students also perceived the tool as beneficial because it provided immediate feedback, supported independent practice, and increased opportunities for repeated pronunciation practice. On the other hand, there were some problems with using the tool, especially regarding mistakes in the transcription due to varying ways people say words, how fast someone speaks, and the amount of noise in the classroom. This research concludes that Gemini Voice-to-Text can facilitate pronunciation awareness through self-correction when its feedback is critically interpreted by students and supported by teacher guidance.

PENERAPAN FLIPPED CLASSROOM BERBASIS VIDEO ANIMASI UNTUK MENINGKATKAN PEMAHAMAN KONSEP MATERI PECAHAN KELAS III SD NEGERI 077279 SI’ŐFABANUA
abstractText: Conceptual understanding of fractions among third-grade elementary school students remains a challenge because the topic is abstract and teacher-centered instruction provides limited opportunities for students to study materials independently and actively. The initial condition in Grade III of SD Negeri 077279 Si’őfabanua showed that only 4 of 21 students (19%) achieved the school mastery criterion of 70, with a class average of 60. This study aimed to describe the implementation of an animated video-based flipped classroom and determine its improvement in students’ conceptual understanding of fractions. The study employed Classroom Action Research based on the Kemmis and McTaggart model and was conducted in two cycles. Each cycle consisted of planning, action, observation, and reflection. The participants were 21 third-grade students, consisting of 10 boys and 11 girls. Data were collected through conceptual understanding tests, teacher and student activity observations, student response questionnaires, and documentation. The data were analyzed descriptively using mean scores and learning mastery percentages. The results showed that the average score increased from 60 in the pre-cycle to 68 in Cycle I and 76 in Cycle II. Learning mastery increased from 19% in the pre-cycle to 57% in Cycle I and 86% in Cycle II. Teacher activity increased from 61% to 88%, while student activity increased from 69% to 82%. Student responses in Cycle II reached 86%, categorized as very positive. Therefore, the implementation of an animated video-based flipped classroom improved students’ conceptual understanding of fractions and encouraged more active participation in learning. title: Exploring Healthcare Professionals' Readiness for Artificial Intelligence in a Resource-Limited Health System: Evidence from Bukavu, Democratic Republic of Congo
abstractText: Introduction: Artificial intelligence (AI) offers opportunities to improve the efficiency of healthcare, but its integration in sub-Saharan Africa faces structural constraints. This exploratory study analyzes the perceptions, expectations, and fears of healthcare professionals in the Ibanda Health Zone (Bukavu, DRC) to document the professional acceptability of these technologies. Methods: The study used a mixed-methods approach: the qualitative exploratory component was based on semi-structured interviews with 11 professionals (physicians, nurses, technicians, managers). The data underwent inductive thematic analysis supplemented by descriptive frequency quantification. Results: Overall attitudes toward AI are favorable, albeit with certain conditions. Despite a predominantly basic or informal understanding of AI (81.8%), perceived benefits include improved diagnostics (72.7%) and data management (63.6%). However, major obstacles persist: lack of formal training (81.8%), internet instability (72.7%), and concerns about the reliability of results (54.5%). AI acceptance is high but conditional, revealing a gap between technological promises and realities on the ground. Training (cited by 90.9% of participants) emerges as the central lever and an ethical prerequisite for safe use. Conclusion : The integration of AI at Ibanda cannot be reduced to a technical issue; it requires strengthening basic infrastructure, a clear regulatory framework, and active involvement of caregivers in the design of tools.

abstractText: Heliogomphus retroflexus (Ris, 1912) is transferred to the genus Microgomphus Selys, 1858 and is herein recognised as M. retroflexus (Ris, 1912), comb. nov., based on evidence from adult and larval morphology and molecular data. New distribution records are reported. The molecular analyses also indicate that the current generic limits of Microgomphus warrant further reassessment. Distribution patterns, sympatry, and knowledge gaps within the genus, as well as their implications for the classification of Oriental gomphids, are also discussed.

Renal effects of chronic D-serine administration in a Parkinson’s disease rat model: evidence for a threshold nephrotoxic dose
abstractText: Abstract D-serine, an endogenous co-agonist at the glycine binding site of NMDA receptor GluN1 subunits, is increasingly studied in Parkinson’s disease, where altered levels have been detected in both patients and animal models. Using a rat model based on α-synuclein overexpression, we evaluated renal effects after eight weeks of daily D-serine administration, alone or in combination with L-DOPA. Given the known acute nephrotoxicity of D-serine in rats, this study addresses the lack of data on chronic exposure. Our results show that a dose of 200 mg/kg induces biological alterations - reflected in growth patterns and water consumption - and peritubular inflammatory infiltrates comparable to the nephrotoxic effect reported after acute treatment. These findings suggest that 200 mg/kg could represent a threshold dose for chronic D-serine administration in rats, providing a useful reference for future studies involving prolonged treatment.

abstractText: Cel pracy Przedstawienie genezy Polskiej e-administracji jest kluczem do zrozumienia procesów i zmian jakie obecnie zachodzą w obszarze transformacji administracji w kierunku jej cyfryzacji. Omówienie najistotniejszych aktów prawnych wpływających na obecny kształt e-administracji i zwrócenie uwagi na kierunki zmian, jakie nastąpią w ty obszarze do 2035 r. Materiał i metody Pracę przygotowano przy pomocy metody historycznoprawnej, dokonując badania genezy i ewolucji transformacji cyfrowej administracji publicznej w oparciu o pierwotne (następnie nowelizowane) regulacje prawne. Wykorzystano również metodę dogmatycznoprawną poprzez analizę przepisów obecnie obowiązujących, orzecznictwa i poglądów doktryny związanych z transformacją administracji w e-administrację. W opracowaniu przytoczono dane statystyczne udostępniana przez Ministerstwo Cyfryzacji. Wyniki Współczesna e administracja charakteryzuje się wysokim stopniem zaawansowania technologicznego oraz rosnącym znaczeniem narzędzi cyfrowych w procesie stosowania prawa administracyjnego. abstractText: Tingkat turnover karyawan PT Tiga Bintang Kreasi, perusahaan produksi dan distribusi tinta di Kota Medan, meningkat dari 3,04% pada 2023 menjadi 11,60% pada 2025, dan pra-survei menunjukkan bahwa banyak karyawan berniat keluar. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh kompensasi, beban kerja, dan pelatihan kerja terhadap turnover intention karyawan. Penelitian kuantitatif asosiatif ini mengumpulkan data melalui kuesioner skala Likert lima poin dari 59 dari 140 karyawan yang dipilih dengan convenience sampling, dengan jumlah sampel ditentukan melalui rumus Slovin, lalu menganalisisnya dengan regresi linear berganda menggunakan SPSS 26. Kompensasi tidak berpengaruh signifikan (B = 0,158; p = 0,084), sehingga H1 tidak didukung. Beban kerja berpengaruh positif dan signifikan (B = 0,352; p = 0,003), sehingga H2 didukung. Pelatihan kerja juga berpengaruh positif dan signifikan (B = 0,371; p = 0,003); karena H3 memprediksi arah negatif, H3 tidak didukung. Ketiga variabel bersama-sama menjelaskan 89,0% variasi turnover intention (F = 147,805; p < 0,001; R² = 0,890). Pengaruh positif pelatihan kerja menunjukkan bahwa pelatihan yang masih terbatas belum diikuti penurunan niat keluar, sehingga pelatihan perlu dikaitkan dengan pengembangan karier dan kebijakan retensi karyawan.

Overall, emotional and social loneliness and their associated factors: a large-scale cross-sectional study of young and middle-aged adults in Germany
abstractText: Abstract Background Loneliness is increasingly recognized as a major public health concern, yet little is known about the distinct patterns and associated factors of emotional and social loneliness during young and middle adulthood. This study examined age-related differences in overall, emotional, and social loneliness and associated sociodemographic, social, health-related, and personality factors among adults in Germany. Methods We analysed nationally representative data from the German Family Demography Panel Study (FReDA), including 14,443 adults aged 18 to 51 years. Loneliness was assessed using the validated De Jong Gierveld Loneliness Short Scale, distinguishing overall, emotional, and social loneliness. Multivariable regression models examined associations with sociodemographic, social, health-related, and personality factors. Analyses were stratified by age and gender. Results High levels of loneliness were common, with 24.3% of participants reporting intense emotional loneliness, 29.6% intense overall loneliness, and 35.8% intense social loneliness. Overall loneliness remained relatively stable across age groups. In contrast, emotional loneliness was lower in older age groups, while social loneliness was higher. Social relationships showed some of the strongest associations with loneliness, particularly social loneliness: discussing personal matters within one’s social network (β = -0.32, 95% CI -0.37 to -0.28) and having a partner (β = -0.21, 95% CI -0.26 to -0.16) were associated with lower social loneliness, while first-generation migration background was associated with higher social loneliness (β = 0.31, 95% CI 0.24 to 0.38). Mental health burdens were consistently associated with higher loneliness, especially emotional loneliness, with depressed mood showing the strongest association (β = 0.22, 95% CI 0.17 to 0.27). Among personality traits, agreeableness was associated with lower social loneliness (β = -0.19, 95% CI -0.22 to -0.17), whereas neuroticism was associated with higher emotional loneliness (β = 0.17, 95% CI 0.14 to 0.20). Gender differences were generally small, as were associations with physical health conditions. Conclusions Loneliness in young and middle adulthood is multidimensional, with emotional and social loneliness showing distinct age-related patterns and associated factors. Social relationships showed some of the strongest associations with lower loneliness, while mental health burdens and first-generation migration background were associated with higher loneliness. Public health strategies may benefit from considering different loneliness dimensions and psychosocial contexts.

title: Pengaruh Sistem Informasi Akuntansi dan Kompetensi Pengguna Sistem terhadap Kinerja Karyawan pada Bank SulutGo Cabang Gorontalo
abstractText: This study aims to analyze the effect of Accounting Information Systems and System User Competence on Employee Performance at Bank SulutGo Gorontalo Branch. This research employed a quantitative approach using a survey method. The population consisted of all employees of Bank SulutGo Gorontalo Branch, with a sample of 40 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using multiple linear regression analysis with the assistance of IBM SPSS Statistics software. The results indicate that the Accounting Information System has no significant effect on Employee Performance. In contrast, System User Competence has a positive and significant effect on Employee Performance. Furthermore, the simultaneous test results reveal that Accounting Information Systems and System User Competence jointly have a positive and significant effect on Employee Performance at Bank SulutGo Gorontalo Branch. These findings suggest that improving employee performance requires not only adequate information system support but also strong user competence to ensure that the system can be utilized optimally in supporting the company's operational activities. The study concludes that System User Competence is a more dominant factor in improving Employee Performance than the Accounting Information System when examined partially. Therefore, Bank SulutGo Gorontalo Branch should continuously enhance employee competence through training and the development of information system utilization skills to support performance improvement.

title: Comparative Analysis of Social Media Discourse Structures on Appearance Management for Women with Disabilities: Focusing on Text Mining of Naver, Instagram, and YouTube
abstractText: This study examined platform-specific structures of social media discourse related to appearance management among women with disabilities across Naver, Instagram, and YouTube. Appearance management among women with disabilities extends beyond beautification to encompass multidimensional issues related to welfare, accessibility, and self-expression. Data were collected over a three-year period (January 2023–December 2025) using combinations of search terms related to women, disability, appearance management, and beauty. The data were analyzed using text mining, keyword analysis, word cloud visualization, semantic network analysis, and CONCOR clustering. After data refinement, 7,411 Naver documents, 1,240 Instagram posts, and text metadata from 302 YouTube videos were collected, and the integrated text metadata of 159 videos were included in the final analysis. Naver showed the highest network density (0.4474), with discourse primarily structured around policy, welfare, support, and education; Instagram (density = 0.3211) showed discourse centered on disability, barrier-free accessibility, welfare centers, beauty practices, and volunteering; and YouTube (density = 0.3000) showed discourse emphasizing disability types, education, welfare, healthcare, and beauty-related support. CONCOR analysis identified four discourse clusters on each platform, although their compositions differed substantially across platforms, with institution- and welfare-oriented clusters on Naver, practice- and accessibility-oriented clusters on Instagram, and a relatively broad education-and-beauty-support cluster on YouTube. Across the three platforms, disability- and beauty-related keywords occupied central positions in the semantic networks, whereas the surrounding keyword structures differed across platforms. The findings suggest that platform-specific content structures and communication affordances may be associated with differences in the organization of online discourse related to disability and beauty, providing empirical insights for the development of platform-specific beauty support programs and digital welfare strategies.

title: Teachers' Creativity In Developing Kamishibai Media To Enhance Disaster Awareness Among Elementary School Students
abstractText: Both Indonesia and Japan are situated in the Pacific Ring of Fire, characterized by high vulnerability to natural disasters. However, the implementation of disaster education in Indonesian elementary schools continues to face challenges, including the scarcity of contextual visual aids and the prevalence of one-way lecture methods. Kamishibai, a traditional Japanese visual storytelling art, offers substantial potential as an alternative instructional medium that synthesizes visual power, oral narration, and interactive theatrical expression to concretize abstract hazard concepts for young learners. This study aims to analyze teachers' creativity in designing Kamishibai media and to evaluate its effectiveness in disaster mitigation instruction. This research employed a quantitative descriptive evaluative survey approach. The study involved 36 educators across various educational levels, including elementary schools, kindergartens, junior high schools, and special education schools in West Java. Data collection utilized a Kamishibai media evaluation questionnaire comprising 12 items on a 1–5 Likert scale, open-ended questions regarding prior mitigation teaching practices, and visual documentation of the Kamishibai media produced by the teachers. Data were analyzed using univariate descriptive statistics to determine frequency distributions, satisfaction percentages, and mean scores. Results: The evaluation of Kamishibai media implementation yielded an overall grand mean score of 4.54 out of 5.00 (90.7% satisfaction rate). The highest ratings were achieved for the medium's capacity to concretize abstract disaster concepts (mean = 4.78; 100% positive response) and to facilitate structured content delivery (mean = 4.72; 100% positive response). The instructional materials developed by teachers during the workshop demonstrated diverse contextual mitigation themes, such as a flood scenario entitled "When the Flood Comes," earthquake simulations emphasizing the "drop, cover, and hold on" technique, as well as landslide mitigation and hillside environmental conservation. Furthermore, 97.2% of teachers deemed Kamishibai significantly more effective than conventional lectures, capable of fostering active classroom discussion (mean = 4.67), and recommended its sustained implementation in disaster-resilient school programs (mean = 4.61). Kamishibai media grounded in teacher creativity has proven to be highly effective, communicative, and accommodating of diverse student learning styles, making it an exemplary instructional aid for early disaster preparedness education in elementary schools.

title: Blended Learning as a Pedagogical Ecology: Relational-Regulatory Functions in the Internalization of Pancasila Values and the Strengthening of Good Character
abstractText: Blended learning (BL) has become increasingly established in higher education, yet research has focused more on effectiveness, engagement, and learning regulation than on how face-to-face and online learning jointly facilitate value internalization. In Pancasila Education, this issue matters because learning outcomes extend beyond knowledge of values to students’ decision-making and relationships. This exploratory qualitative study analyzed open-ended questionnaire responses from 67 Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia students using directed qualitative content analysis, complemented by a contextual review of learning materials and activities available through SPOT UPI. The findings reveal four patterns. First, students perceived face-to-face learning primarily as a relational space for dialogue, clarification, deliberation, and collaboration. At the same time, online learning served mainly as a regulatory space for flexibility, access to materials, time management, and independence. These functions complemented each other but were not exclusive. Second, value internalization became visible when Pancasila shifted from content to be understood into a basis for decision-making, respect for differences, rule compliance, and responsibility. Third, good character was associated with relational pathways toward justice and collaboration and self-regulatory pathways toward discipline, responsibility, and work ethic. Social support, digital culture, and LMS reliability influenced these processes. Fourth, discrepancies between ideal values and reality triggered moral reflection for some students, described as productive moral dissonance. The study interprets BL as an architecture of relational-regulatory functions and suggests connecting social interaction, self-regulation, authentic cases, reflection, process assessment, and reliable digital infrastructure in Pancasila Education. Keywords: Pancasila education, Value internalization, Blended learning; Good character; Higher education
